> 五色令人目盲；五音令人耳聾；五味令人口爽.

Chapter 12 is a list of losses: colors blind the eye, sounds deafen the ear, flavors dull the palate, hunting drives the heart wild, rare goods obstruct conduct.

Read as asceticism, it is a chapter about denying the senses. Read precisely, it is a chapter about who is in charge of the receiving end.

## 受於身，不如治於身

Colors, sounds, and flavors are not evils. They are objects that exist in the world; they arrive at the senses passively, whether you asked for them or not. There is no moral quality in a color.

What the chapter describes is the collapse of the receiving end. 盲 is not literally blindness; it is the loss of the ability to distinguish — the eye that has been hit with saturation all day can no longer see subtlety. 聾, 爽 (a damaged palate) work the same way.

So the instruction is not to seal the door. It is to take back control of how the door receives.

## 五色: 觀而不惰

Look, without going slack. The failure is not looking; it is letting the looking be done for you — feeds, tiles, colors engineered to hold attention. Once the eye is trained to wait for the next hit, the capacity for quiet looking is gone.

## 五音: 享而不溺

Enjoy, without drowning. Music is not the problem. The problem is volume as a default state: when sound is always on, silence stops being a place you can enter and becomes an absence you have to tolerate.

## 五味: 品而不酗

Taste, without bingeing. 爽 is the specific damage of intensity: the palate calibrated for strong flavor can no longer register the subtle. This is the mechanism behind the observation that people who eat richly stop being able to taste.

## 馳騁畋獵，令人心發狂

The fourth line shifts from senses to motion. Hunting is not a metaphor for entertainment; it is the structure of pursuit — the chase that organizes the whole organism around a moving target. The 狂 is not madness in the clinical sense, it is the state of a mind that cannot stop moving because the target has not stopped.

## 難得之貨，令人行妨

The fifth shifts to conduct. 妨 is obstruction: rare goods obstruct behavior. The rarity is what does it — the object is not needed, but because it is hard to get, acquiring it reorganizes your actions around itself.

## 為腹不為目

> 是以聖人為腹不為目，故去彼取此.

王弼's note is the cleanest reading available: 為腹者，以物養己；為目者，以物役己. The belly uses things to nourish a person. The eye is used by things to drive a person.

The distinction is not between body and eye, and not between coarse and refined. It is between the mode where the object serves the person and the mode where the person serves the object.

So 去彼取此 is not a list of things to renounce. It is a change of direction: from being driven by what is displayed to being nourished by what is needed.

## A test

Take the last hour before bed. Count how many things arrived at your eyes and ears because you chose them, and how many because they were placed where you would hit them. The ratio is usually the chapter's argument, without any commentary needed.
